correctness.rationale: The derivative of a stopped-Poisson row has nonterminal entries p_(k-1)-p_k and terminal entry p_(n-i-1). The absolute row sum is twice the largest retained Poisson mass by unimodality and zero row sum; the nonterminal column sum is the variation of the truncated mass sequence starting at zero, and the terminal column sum is F_(n-1). This gives both formulas, including mode ties, n=1, and the real/complex counting norms. The piecewise time-weighted mode grows strictly to n and then decays. For the absorbing-column optimizer, F_(n-1)/(t p_(n-1)) is a strictly decreasing sum of inverse powers, so it crosses one exactly once. Stirling at t=n-c sqrt(n log n) gives t p_(n-1)~n^((1-c^2)/2)/sqrt(2 pi), while F tends to 1 (even Chebyshev gives an O(1/log n) upper tail there); derivative signs bracket the optimizer for c on either side of 1. At the optimizer p_n=F/n and the tail geometric bound loses only O(sqrt(n/log n)) in the time-weighted norm. The nonterminal branch is bounded by the infinity-mode expression, hence its supremum is O(sqrt n) and cannot compete for large n. The spectrum follows from triangularity.
residual_risks: No claim of an all-n absorbing-column optimizer or interior-p law; the replay is finite, not the proof of the asymptotic.
